Agreed to run a 1-week benchmark using Lumen prompts and share pricing for a pilot.

Optimize suggestions: batching, quant and caching
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood Product), Priya Nair (Lumen CTO), Daniel Holt (Lumen ML), Sofia Ruiz (Lumen Infra), Ken Patel (Lumen Data)

[00:00:00] Alyssa (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro, I'm Alyssa, I'll run the demo, Marcus will handle the bench bits and Diego has the catalog roadmap notes.
[00:00:12] Priya (Lumen CTO): Thanks, Alyssa. we wanted to focus on how you pick open models, how you read the bench numbers, and what would be involved to run a pilot in our VPC.
[00:00:25] Marcus (Redwood SE): Great, that's exactly what we'll cover. quick agenda: catalog walkthrough, compatibility matrix, bench interpretation, then discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private. sound OK?
[00:00:36] Daniel (Lumen ML): Yep, and please call out quantized variants—latency on small gpus is critical for us.
[00:00:44] Alyssa: noted. one other ask, if you could share a small prompt set after the call we'll slot it into the bench.
[00:00:50] Priya: we'll do that.

-- Catalog demo --
[00:01:10] Marcus: opening the Console, top-left is the model catalog. you can filter by task—generation, chat, embeddings—also by license and throughput target. i'm going to filter to open models and show the compatibility matrix view.
[00:01:28] Marcus: so here each model has a set of model cards; the matrix maps model to runtime kernels and recommended instance classes. for ex, Mistral-7B-quant is marked as "quantized-ready" with good T4 perf. note: transcription may show Mistral as "Mistral" or sometimes mis- spelled, but you'll see details.
[00:01:50] Sofia (Lumen Infra): can you show how you map to dedicated pools? we need guaranteed qps.
[00:01:58] Marcus: yep, dedicated mapping is in the right column—pool types and min vcores. you can pin model variants to a dedicated pool to prevent noisy neighbor issues. also autoscale policies are attached.

[00:02:20] Diego (Redwood Product): quick note on the matrix logic—it's a decision graph under the hood: compatibility checks by architecture, sequence length, and kernel availability. we also annotate quant support and fallback compatibility when a kernel isn't available.
[00:02:36] Ken (Lumen Data): what does fallback mean operationally? if T4 is saturated do you auto-fall back to slower CPU?
[00:02:43] Marcus: not CPU—usually a compatible variant on a different GPU class or a slightly lower-precision quant variant. fallbacks are policy driven: cost-priority or latency-priority.

-- Benchmarks and Interpretations --
[00:03:10] Marcus: switching to bench tab—here's a preloaded bench using our sample prompt suite. columns: p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and kernel mapping. remember bench numbers are workload dependent.
[00:03:28] Daniel: the cost numbers look lower than what we saw on our in-house tests?
[00:03:33] Marcus: likely because our bench uses continuous batching and KV cache reuse where applicable—if your prompts are mostly independent the gains will be less. also note we run with our quant kernels which shift perf/cost.
[00:03:50] Alyssa: one thing to watch: the UI shows an expected delta when you change sequence length; that's critical for pricing.
[00:03:58] Priya: about quantization—how much does that affect quality for code/finance prompts?
[00:04:05] Diego: depends on model class; we'll flag models where 4-bit quant shows small regressions on safety/accuracy evals. we also recommend spot-checks with your test suite.
[00:04:18] Daniel: ok, spot-checks good. can you export the bench CSV so we can run our numbers?
[00:04:22] Marcus: yes, export button on the top-right. i'll attach the exact export as a follow-up.

[00:05:00] Speaker 1: (murmur)

-- Optimize features and recommendations --
[00:05:20] Marcus: now Optimize tab—this is our cost/perf recommender. it suggests batch size, cache TTL, quant profile and routing policy. example: for Mistral-like models it suggested batch=8 and prefix-KV caching with 30s TTL, saving ~18% cost in this bench.
[00:05:40] Priya: is that suggestion safe for low-latency requests? we have sub-150ms SLO for some endpoints.
[00:05:48] Marcus: Optimize balances latency and cost; it will propose latency-friendly configs if you set latency SLO. we can lock SLO in the route policy so suggestions respect that.
[00:06:00] Ken: how do we test that in our environment? we prefer to run in our VPC if possible.
[00:06:07] Alyssa: two paths—hosted pilot with private data controls, or Redwood Private deployed into your VPC/on-prem. both support the same Optimize tooling; the difference is traffic egress and control plane placement.

[00:06:30] Sofia: on the Private side, what about key management? KMS/HSM?
[00:06:36] Diego: we integrate with customer KMS and HSM; for on-prem there are options for HSM-backed keys. audit logs and RBAC are also included.

-- API and SDK quick show --
[00:07:05] Marcus: quick API snippet—POST /v1/generate with model id. SDK shows streaming and function calling. note: if you use routing policies you can pin calls by model id or by tag, so the same API call can route to different variants in prod.
[00:07:30] Daniel: can we programmatically read the compatibility matrix? we want to build an internal selector.
[00:07:35] Marcus: yes, there's an API endpoint that returns the matrix and model metadata. we'll provide the spec in the follow-up. small caveat—matrix fields may change between releases; we version them.

-- Live scenario: selecting shortlist for Lumen checkout flow --
[00:08:05] Alyssa: let's walk through a concrete example. Lumen needs a small chat assistant for account questions with 300ms target and low cost. what models would you shortlist?
[00:08:15] Daniel: we prefer open models to avoid licensing.
[00:08:18] Marcus: filter open models, then sort by p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens. shortlist shows: Mistral-7B-quant, Llama-2-13B-pt-quant, and a trimmed Falcon variant. the matrix shows kernel fit: Mistral->T4/A100 quant good, Llama-2-13B->A100 best, Falcon->A10x.
[00:08:40] Priya: that Llama-2 13B was surprising—wasn't it usually heavier?
[00:08:44] Diego: our kernel mapping has a specialized fp16 path for that checkpoint, plus KV cache optimization reduces p95 for typical chat lengths.
[00:08:56] Ken: for our SREs, what's the expected tail behavior during spikes?
[00:09:02] Marcus: routing policies support burst capacity and can fallback to a lower-cost region or variant; console shows simulated burst headroom. for strict SLOs we recommend dedicated pools.

-- Discussion: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private --
[00:09:30] Priya: cost-wise, what's the rough delta between hosted usage and dedicated?
[00:09:37] Alyssa: hosted is pay-as-you-go; for sustained throughput a dedicated reserved pool often lowers unit cost by 30-50% depending on commitment. we can model your expected qps and give a compare.
[00:09:50] Daniel: any hidden charges for Optimize or bench runs?
[00:09:53] Marcus: bench runs on Redwood hosted are included for pilots; Optimize suggestions are part of the platform. large-scale long-retained observability is an add-on. we'll call out specifics in pricing.

[00:10:20] Priya: compliance—SOC2/ISO and audit logs—are those turned on for hosted pilots?
[00:10:26] Diego: yes, we can enable audit logs and SSO for pilots; SOC2 docs are in the security pack we'll share. for private/on-prem we can meet stricter needs.

-- Technical deep dive: kernels, quant, and kernel mapping --
[00:11:00] Marcus: diving deeper—kernel mapping is driven by a compatibility engine that tests kernels across sequence lengths and tokenization shapes; we maintain a matrix per model and hardware family. the console shows the recommended kernel and expected memory profile.
[00:11:20] Daniel: are those kernel picks deterministic? we handle incompatible kernels with fallbacks.
[00:11:25] Marcus: yes deterministic per release; if you pin a model version you get a stable mapping.
[00:11:30] Sofia: any concerns with KV cache usage and multi-tenant pools?
[00:11:35] Marcus: KV cache is partitioned per customer session; on shared pools cache eviction and TTL policies keep it safe—on dedicated you get isolated caches.

-- Noise: transcription hiccups --
[00:12:00] Speaker 2: (background) yep

-- Bench export and interpretation example --
[00:12:20] Marcus: exporting the bench CSV now, columns include bench id, model, kernel, seq len, p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and notes. i'll attach it. note: CSV sometimes lists kernel names with hyphens that our UI normalizes.
[00:12:45] Priya: when you ran these on T4 did you enable tensor cores or any special flags?
[00:12:51] Marcus: yes tensor cores and our custom kernel path. we also experimented with 3-bit quant on a few models; results varied.

[00:13:20] Daniel: for our test harness, can we call the bench API to re-run identical configs?
[00:13:24] Marcus: absolutely, bench as code. i'll include the exact bench config in the follow-up.

-- Questions from Lumen on routing policies and model rollouts --
[00:14:00] Ken: how do rollouts work? can we A/B two models for a subset of traffic?
[00:14:05] Diego: yes, we support canary and weighted rollouts, and automatic rollback on quality regressions if you tie a prompt set to an eval.
[00:14:15] Priya: if a new model causes hallucinations, can we auto-failover?
[00:14:20] Marcus: yes, you can configure auto-fallback to a pinned safe model or to the previous version. the console surface shows recent regressions and evaluation diffs.

[00:14:40] Speaker 3: (laughter)

-- Commercial considerations --
[00:15:05] Alyssa: on pricing, we'll send two options: a hosted pilot with usage cap and a dedicated 3-month pilot with a committment estimate. which is preferable?
[00:15:16] Priya: for initial evaluation hosted pilot is fine; if numbers look good we may move to dedicated.
[00:15:23] Alyssa: great, we'll do that path.

-- Implementation concerns --
[00:16:00] Sofia: VPC peering, IP allowlist, and egress—what's required?
[00:16:05] Marcus: minimal: VPC peering or private link, support for mutual TLS if you want, and an IP allowlist for control-plane callbacks. we'll share a checklist.

[00:16:30] Daniel: about privacy—do you store prompt data? retention policies?
[00:16:35] Diego: default retention is 30 days for hosted; you can opt out and have no retention, or run Private to keep everything in your environment. we'll share the retention options doc.

-- Deeper bench scenario: payment support prompts --
[00:17:10] Marcus: i ran a quick local bench on a payment-related prompt set; Mistral-7B-quant had p95 ~180ms on T4 with batch 8 and caching, cost per 1k tokens $0.09 (est). Llama-2-13B on A100 had p95 ~120ms but cost $0.25 per 1k. tradeoff is clear: lower cost vs lower latency.
[00:17:40] Daniel: those numbers are helpful. are the numbers including the cost of KV cache memory?
[00:17:45] Marcus: yes they're amortized into the per-token cost in the bench.

[00:18:10] Priya: one more on quant: did you observe any critical failure modes with finance prompts?
[00:18:15] Marcus: in some small tests 4-bit quant changed trailing numerical precision in rare cases; we recommend targeted evals on numeric fidelity-sensitive prompts.

-- Roadmap mention and product gaps --
[00:18:40] Diego: roadmap: improving auto-quant recommendations, better kernel fallbacks for Edge GPUs, and expanded model vetting metadata (e.g., eval signal per-dataset). note: this area is evolving.
[00:18:55] Ken: any ETA on expanded vetting metadata?
[00:19:00] Diego: Q3 roadmap, but we'll confirm dates in a follow-up.

-- Closing: recap and next steps --
[00:19:30] Alyssa: recap: we'll send pricing and pilot contract, Marcus will run the 1-week bench using your prompt set, Diego will attach the compatibility matrix export and security docs. we'll plan a follow-up to review bench results.
[00:19:50] Priya: good. can we aim to have bench results in two weeks?
[00:19:55] Marcus: yes aiming for two weeks, realistically 7-10 days once we have prompts and access.
[00:20:02] Alyssa: thanks everyone. i'll share meeting notes and next steps.
[00:20:07] Daniel: thanks all.

-- End of recording (note: transcript may contain minor mis-attributions and ASR typos like 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache')
